successors.name: Neo-Hittite states
successors.text: Kammanu, 'a Luwian (Neo-Hittite) state centred on Melid', the infobox successor

ledger.x: c. 1400 BC (first dated mention): Isuwa stands against Hatti. 'Suppiluliuma I recorded that Isuwa turned hostile in his father's time' (Tudhaliya II, c. 1400 BC). The page gives no founding date; it says Isuwa was 'under Hittite sovereignty from c. 1600 BC', so this is a bridging judgment at the first hostile act.

c. 1400 BC (bridged): Isuwa is Mitanni's vassal. The Suppiluliuma I page has the Hittites 'overrunning its vassal Isuwa' in the assault on Mitanni (undated); the Isuwa page has Mitanni fuel the hostility and Shaushtatar apparently fighting Arnuwanda I with Isuwan support (undated).

c. 1350 BC: Suppiluliuma I breaks Isuwa. 'He crossed the Euphrates and entered the land of Isuwa with his troops' (c. 1350 BC); the Suppiluliuma I page puts it in the assault on Mitanni, 'overrunning its vassal Isuwa', and gives no year (his reign is 'c. 1350-1322 BC').

c. 1350 BC: Isuwa becomes a Hittite vassal. 'He claimed Isuwa as his subject'; Hittite letters name Ehli-sharruma as king of Isuwa in the 13th century BC and the king Ari-Sharruma is Kilushepa's husband.
c. 1180 BC: the Hittite empire falls. 'After the fall of the Hittite empire in the early twelfth century BC' a new state arises in Isuwa's place; the hittites dossier ends the empire c. 1180.

c. 1180 BC: Isuwa is succeeded by Kammanu. Infobox 'Succeeded by: Kammanu', a Luwian state centred on Melid, which paid tribute to Tiglath-Pileser I (1115-1077 BC) and was sacked by Sargon II in 712 BC.

wars.name: Hostility of Isuwa under Tudhaliya II and Arnuwanda I
wars.outcome: 'The land of Isuwa became hostile' in Tudhaliya II's time (c.

wars.name: Suppiluliuma I's assault on Mitanni and Isuwa
wars.outcome: Suppiluliuma I 'launched a direct assault on Mittani, overrunning its vassal Isuwa' and took Washukanni; Isuwa became his subject.

certainty.note: Only the Euphrates and the Tunceli/Elazig plain are named; no frontier is described.
